title: NTSB finds 'no evidence' of Mar-a-Lago connection after Florida jet crash kills nine people
summary: The Learjet 60's left elevator was found miles from the Palm Beach County crash site, adding to evidence the jet broke apart before killing all nine aboard.
story: National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman shares during a news conference Tuesday that a critical piece of the private jet that plunged into a Florida neighborhood Sunday was found several miles from the impact site.

A critical piece of the private jet that plunged into a Florida neighborhood was found miles from the impact site, federal investigators revealed Tuesday as crews prepared to drain the crater left by the crash that killed nine people.

Asked about the crash occurring less than 10 miles from President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago home and any potential connection to Secret Service operations, National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman dismissed a link.
"There is no evidence of connection. Purely coincidence," he said.
FORMER NFL STAR SAYS HE PREVIOUSLY FLEW ON PRIVATE JET THAT CRASHED IN FLORIDA: 'ABSOLUTELY DEVASTATED'
Investigators work at the site of a plane crash in Greenacres, Fla., Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)
Most of the jet’s left elevator, a movable part of the tail that helps control the aircraft’s nose up or down, was recovered between 1.3 and 3.8 miles from the crash site, Chapman said.
The discovery adds to evidence that the aircraft began breaking apart before impact. The elevator is a movable surface on the aircraft’s tail that helps control whether its nose points up or down.
TEXAS FAMILY OF 4, 20-YEAR-OLD COPILOT AMONG 9 KILLED IN FIERY FLORIDA JET CRASH
A Learjet 60 crashed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday afternoon (Palm Beach County Fire Rescue)
But Chapman said he did not believe the component would have enabled the aircraft to recover even if it had remained attached, given the speed of the jet’s descent.
The Learjet was carrying seven passengers and two crew members from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas when it crashed Sunday, killing everyone aboard.
FAA SEEKS PERMANENT AIRSPACE RESTRICTIONS NEAR TRUMP’S MAR-A-LAGO AS EXPERT WARNS RULES ARE ‘NOT GOOD ENOUGH’

Investigators are now preparing to remove water from the impact crater, where Chapman said they expect to recover additional aircraft components. Given the force of the crash, pieces buried there will likely be small.
Severe weather has hampered some recovery efforts, and weather remains a key focus of the investigation. The cause of the crash has not been determined.
FAA, NTSB INVESTIGATING POSSIBLE VIOLATION OF SAFETY PROTOCOL INVOLVING TRUMP, MARINE ONE

Investigators have also obtained dashcam footage to help reconstruct the aircraft’s final moments, Chapman said. Recovered wreckage is being retained for analysis, and officials urged anyone who encounters debris to leave it untouched and notify authorities.

The crew had reported light clear ice and moderate turbulence while flying at about 35,000 feet before requesting permission to climb to 37,000 feet. Less than 30 seconds after controllers approved the request, the crew reported they were descending and issued a mayday call.
Roughly 600 residents near Military Trail and Cresthaven Boulevard were evacuated after the crash, according to The Palm Beach Post.

Between 40 and 50 people were staying at the Greenacres Community Center, Palm Beach County spokesperson John Jamason told the outlet. County officials were seeking state funding to help displaced residents with housing and transportation while authorities worked at the crash site.
TRUMP HELICOPTER’S RADIO WARNINGS WENT UNHEARD BEFORE CLOSE CALL WITH PASSENGER JET, REPORT SAYS

Officials said during Tuesday’s briefing that Military Trail remained closed in both directions between 10th Avenue North and Purdy Lane. They did not provide a timeline for reopening the road or allowing displaced residents to return home.
Among those killed were Austin technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, 45, his wife, Helen Sharp, 40, and their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2.
NORAD FIGHTER JETS INTERCEPT 2 AIRCRAFT NEAR TRUMP’S GOLF CLUB, 3RD PLANE DELAYS HIS NJ DEPARTURE

Adam Robinson was CEO and co-founder of Retention.com and also led RB2B and MoltSets. His companies remembered him as "a friend, a mentor and a bold, outspoken leader who lived life to the fullest." (Fox News)

Robinson, CEO and co-founder of Retention.com, had celebrated a business milestone in his final LinkedIn post the day of the crash, announcing that RB2B had reached $10 million in annual recurring revenue. He was also preparing for a live business debate scheduled for Tuesday.

"Adam and Helen were devoted parents, and Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were the light of their lives. Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last forever," the families said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.
"Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives. Their loss will be felt deeply by all those who loved them and who they loved in return."
Chapman expressed confidence that investigators would determine what happened and thanked Florida and Palm Beach County authorities and first responders for their assistance.

Officials added that further investigative updates will be posted on the NTSB’s website.
Fox News Digital's Greg Wehner contributed to this report.

title: Retired NYPD officer arrested after 'off with his head' post over Florida mosque expansion
summary: Retired NYPD officer Rodolfo Mienert allegedly posted "off with his head!" on Facebook targeting a Pinellas County commissioner over a mosque vote.
story: During an Oct. 27 Pinellas County Commission meeting, Rodolfo Mienert argued against a mosque expansion. Days later, he was arrested after allegedly calling for the beheading of a commissioner. (Pinellas County Board of County Commissioners)

A retired NYPD officer living in Florida was arrested Monday after authorities say he made a social media post calling for the beheading of a Pinellas County commissioner who recently voted to approve the expansion of a local mosque.

Rodolfo Mienert, who now lives in St. Petersburg, allegedly commented on a Facebook post criticizing Pinellas County Commissioner Brian Scott for supporting a land-use change that would allow the North Pinellas mosque to expand.
According to the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office, the 68-year-old ex-officer called Scott a "Republican turncoat" before writing, "off with his head!"
Mienert posted this Facebook comment under the username "Rudy MineAllmine," according to an affidavit obtained by Fox News Digital.

A booking photo for Rodolfo Mienert, 68, a retired NYPD officer who was arrested Nov. 2, 2026, after allegedly making a post calling for the beheading of Pinellas County Commissioner Brian Scott. (Pinellas County Sheriff's Office)
OHIO MAN CHARGED OVER GRAPHIC THREATS TO KILL TRUMP, BEHEAD GOP LAWMAKER
The account's profile picture shows Bugs Bunny holding a revolver, while its bio reads, "...if I pissed off a libtard today, I'm happy!! no further reply!!"
The last post made by this account reposted a campaign video from Scott, accompanied with the message: "DO NOT vote for this person, he voted FOR a mosque."
Detectives traced the IP address of the account that made the post to Mienert, who later confirmed the account was his.

A headshot photo for Brian Scott, a Pinellas County Commissioner. Last month, Scott voted in favor of a proposal that would allow a local mosque to expand. (Photography provided courtesy of Pinellas County Communications Department)
MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY POSTING GRUESOME DEATH THREATS AGAINST KRISTI NOEM, PAM BONDI ON SOCIAL MEDIA
Mienert told detectives he is "very vocal and not afraid to share his opinion" on political issues and said he called Scott a "turncoat" because of his vote to approve the mosque expansion.
Mienert also told detectives he had attended an Oct. 27 County Commission meeting where residents discussed the mosque issue at length.
During that meeting, he said he escaped New York to "beautiful Florida" and claimed the growing footprint of the mosque would damage the environment and make traffic worse.

Rodolfo Mienert is seen speaking during a Pinellas County Commission meeting on Oct. 27, 2026, days before he was arrested. Mienert, along with many others, criticized the commission's decision to approve the mosque expansion. (Pinellas County Commission)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Mienert was arrested and charged with one felony count of a written or electronic threat to kill, an offense that carries a maximum of 15 years in prison in Florida.

In a statement, Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri said that "threatening to cut off the head of a county commissioner because of his vote on a land issue is intolerable and we will strictly enforce the law against anyone who makes threats of this nature."

Mienert, who retired as a sergeant after 22 years with the New York Police Department, remains in the Pinellas County Jail, according to records reviewed by Fox News Digital. He is set to appear in court Tuesday afternoon.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: Missouri State Highway Patrol captures convicted murderer who escaped Tennessee prison
summary: Jacob Allen Morley broke out of the Northwest Correctional Complex last week before Missouri state troopers tracked down the escaped murderer.
story: Investigators say an escaped murderer in Tennessee could be in connection with an armed bank robbery in Deerfield, Wisconsin. Suspect Jacob Morley reportedly broke out of prison, where he was serving a life sentence.
Missouri state troopers have captured an escaped convict who broke free from a Tennessee prison last week, a highway patrol spokesperson told Fox News Digital Tuesday.
Jacob Allen Morley broke out of the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, on Oct. 25, officials said previously. He was serving a life prison sentence for murder.

After his escape, he allegedly stole a truck, and authorities said they used FLOCK cameras to help track it down. As state troopers closed in on him, they say he tried to veer off the road and got stuck.
He was arrested without further incident about two hours after police first caught wind of his possible location, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol.
TENNESSEE INMATE CONVICTED OF MURDER ESCAPES FROM PRISON, STEALS PICKUP TRUCK, MANHUNT UNDERWAY: OFFICIALS
A split image showing Jacob Morley before his Tennessee prison escape and after his recapture in Missouri. (Tennessee DOC, Missouri Highway Patrol)

"On November 3, 2026, at approximately 9:30 a.m., the Patrol’s Missouri Information Analysis Center and Troop A Communications received information from the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation that Morley may be traveling westbound on Interstate 70 near Independence," the Missouri State Highway Patrol said in a statement. "The suspect vehicle was located using FLOCK cameras, and officers began to deploy to the area. With additional use of FLOCK cameras, the suspect vehicle was located by undercover officers traveling south on Missouri 291 in Liberty."
SEND US A TIP
The stolen Ford F-350 authorities say escaped Tennessee inmate Jacob Morley drove after fleeing prison was found abandoned in Marion, Illinois. (Tennessee Bureau of Investigation)

Police from several different local and federal agencies, including the Kansas City Police Department, Independence Police Department, Career Criminal Task Force, Homeland Security Investigations, and the United States Marshals Service, assisted in the effort to surround and capture him, MSHP said.

Staff at the prison noticed Morley was unaccounted for at around 11:30 p.m., and a review of surveillance footage subsequently revealed him crossing through the prison's perimeter fence. According to Tennessee Highway Patrol dispatch audio, Morley was last seen at the prison around 4 p.m. Sunday.
CONVICTED MURDERER GOT OVER 5-HOUR HEAD START AFTER PRISON ESCAPE BEFORE LOCAL POLICE WERE NOTIFIED: OFFICIAL

Morley was arrested in 2022 in connection with the murder of a man named Cody Birchfield. Police had initially arrested Morley near the border with North Carolina and later found Birchfield's body under Morley's home. In 2025, he was convicted at the end of a trial that included his ex-girlfriend testifying that, "he f---ing killed him."

Tennessee authorities later publicly thanked the public and the Missouri Highway Patrol for their help recapturing the killer, who was previously convicted of first-degree murder, burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism.

Jacob Allen Morley, 28, who was serving a life sentence for murder, escaped from Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, prompting a manhunt involving state and federal authorities. (Tennessee Department of Correction)

title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Mangione’s new argument to escape NY murder case: Same gun, same killing, same prosecution
summary: Luigi Mangione's lawyers argue murder and federal stalking charges target the same evil, pressing a double jeopardy defense to dismiss New York charges.
story: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal charges as his defense attorneys aggressively move to dismiss state murder charges in New York. Former prosecutor Nancy Grace joins 'Fox & Friends Weekend' to dissect the legal maneuvering surrounding the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

Luigi Mangione's lawyers are doubling down on their double jeopardy defense in their fight to have the admitted assassin spared from New York murder charges after admitting to what they say was essentially the same crime in federal court.
Murder is the same evil as stalking with intent to kill — and then killing, they argued.

The claims came in response to Manhattan prosecutors who have asked a New York judge to reject his bid to drop his state-level charges following a federal guilty plea in which he admitted to assassinating UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, a 50-year-old father of two who Mangione shot in the back outside a Hilton hotel in the middle of the Big Apple.
BRAVE WIDOW OF SLAIN UNITEDHEALTHCARE CEO BRIAN THOMPSON COMES FACE TO FACE WITH LUIGI MANGIONE FOR FIRST TIME
Luigi Mangione appears in Manhattan Supreme Court for a hearing in the murder case filed against him for killing UHC Brian Thompson on Sept. 16, 2025. (Curtis Means for DailyMail/Pool)

Prosecutors have said that since Mangione was not prosecuted for federal firearms offenses, there is no double jeopardy if the state level ones remain on the table. They argued that the murder charges should still go forward because although Mangione admitted to killing Thompson, that's not the same "harm or evil" involved in the federal stalking charges. And they argued that even though Mangione withdrew a potential "extreme emotional disturbance" defense specific to Empire State law, that doesn't mean the federal case prevented him from using it.
Mangione's lawyers, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Marc Agnifilo and Jacob Kaplan, attacked all three arguments in a reply made public over the weekend.
LUIGI MANGIONE PLEA BUZZ RAISES POTENTIAL PAUL MANAFORT PROBLEM FOR PROSECUTORS
READ the defense reply:
First, they argued that although the federal firearms charges were dismissed, he was still "prosecuted" for them, putting him at risk of double jeopardy.
"The statutory definition of being 'prosecuted' for an offense does not require that the defendant plead guilty to that specific offense," Mangione's lawyers wrote.
LUIGI MANGIONE HEARING SET FOR FRIDAY STIRS PLEA DEAL SPECULATION IN HIS FEDERAL CASE
Their client pleaded guilty to two federal charges, although he'd initially faced more.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"In other words, when Mangione pleaded guilty to the federal indictment, the criminal action in which he had been charged with possession and use of the firearm was terminated for statutory double jeopardy purposes," they wrote.

A member of the NYPD Crime Scene Unit takes a picture of a shell casing found at the scene where the CEO of UnitedHealthcare, Brian Thompson, was shot and killed in Midtown Manhattan, in New York City, Dec. 4, 2024. (REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton)

They also argued that stalking Thompson with intent to kill him is the same "core misconduct" as murdering him. In order to get around New York's double jeopardy law, which is more restrictive than the U.S. Constitution, prosecutors need to show that the state charges are meant to prevent different "harms or evils" than the federal ones he already pleaded guilty to.

UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, left, pictured in a corporate headshot. He was killed on Dec. 4, 2024, outside a Manhattan hotel while on his way to a shareholder conference. The suspect, Luigi Mangione, is pictured in court on the right. (Businesswire, Steven Hirsch for New York Post via Pool)

"One of the harms clearly addressed by the expansive federal stalking statute is stalking with the intent to kill and resulting in the killing of the person stalked," Mangione's lawyers wrote. "It is a statute that, like a state murder statute, is intended to keep people safe from being murdered — the oldest crime there is."
LUIGI MANGIONE'S TEAM FIRES BACK AT PLEA DEAL REPORT, CALLS LEAKS THREAT TO FAIR TRIAL

They argued that while the federal stalking charge includes other elements, including interstate travel and the use of electronic communications, they are "not related" to the core evil of the crime, which is killing someone.

Luigi Mangione appears in Manhattan Supreme Court for a hearing in the murder case filed against him for killing UHC Brian Thompson on Sept. 16, 2025. (Curtis Means for DailyMail/Pool)

"Travel and electronics are not the evils or harms being prevented," they wrote. "The federal government does have an interest, however, in preventing people from [traveling] or using electronics as part of the crime of killing another person, or intending to do so. That is what makes the stalking statute similar to the murder statute in terms of the evils or harms both are looking to prevent."

title: Austin tech founder killed with wife and children in Florida jet crash had reached a $10M business milestone
summary: Adam Robinson's final LinkedIn post celebrated RB2B hitting $10 million in annual recurring revenue and teased a live debate he would never attend.
story: Fox News correspondent Christina Coleman reports on the investigation into a private jet crash in Palm Beach County, Florida, that killed nine people on 'Hannity.'

An Austin tech founder who was killed alongside his wife and two young children in a fiery Florida jet crash had just celebrated a major business milestone and was making plans for a live event Tuesday in what became his final LinkedIn post.

Adam Robinson, 45, his wife, Helen Sharp, 40, and their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were among nine people killed Sunday when the Learjet 60 carrying them from Austin to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas plunged into a Palm Beach County neighborhood.
On the day of the crash, Robinson wrote that RB2B had reached $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR).
FLORIDA PLANE CRASH VICTIMS IDENTIFIED AFTER 9 PEOPLE KILLED IN FIERY WRECK

Adam Robinson and his wife, Helen Sharp, were traveling with their two young children when the Learjet carrying them from Texas to the Bahamas crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Nov. 1. (Courtesy: Facebook)
"RB2B is $10m ARR with 1 FTE," Robinson wrote. "MoltSets is almost $1m ARR."
Two months earlier, Robinson said RB2B was generating $9.5 million in annual recurring revenue and described reaching $10 million with a small team as "the promised land."
Robinson was CEO and co-founder of Retention.com, an Austin-based company that helps businesses identify people who visit their websites and reach them with advertising and marketing.

The company later launched RB2B, which helps businesses identify potential customers visiting their websites. Robinson also led MoltSets, which provides business contact information, including work emails and phone numbers.
PRIVATE JET WITH 9 PEOPLE ON BOARD CRASHES JUST MILES FROM MAR-A-LAGO

Adam Robinson sits on a boat with one of his young children. Robinson, his wife, Helen Sharp, and their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were killed in the Nov. 1 Learjet crash in Palm Beach County, Florida. (Courtesy: Linkedin/ Adam Robinson)
In his final post, Robinson described a debate with friend Jesse Ouellette over whether RB2B and MoltSets should remain separate or be combined.
Robinson wrote that Ouellette believed combining them could reduce customer turnover and double revenue, while he favored keeping the products separate.
"My question: WHY DO I NEED TO DO EITHER OF THOSE THINGS?" Robinson wrote.
"Honestly, I'd be thrilled if RB2B never grew another dollar," he added.
FORMER NFL STAR SAYS HE PREVIOUSLY FLEW ON PRIVATE JET THAT CRASHED IN FLORIDA: 'ABSOLUTELY DEVASTATED'
The two planned to settle their disagreement during a live debate Tuesday on "Claude Did What!!??"
"So we're settling it LIVE," Robinson wrote.
"There's much more to his argument, but I'm saving it for Tuesday," he added. "Grab some popcorn and pick a side."

Adam Robinson was CEO and co-founder of Retention.com and also led RB2B and MoltSets. His companies remembered him as "a friend, a mentor and a bold, outspoken leader who lived life to the fullest." (Fox News)

Robinson never made it to the debate.
The Robinson family was remembered in a joint statement provided to Fox News Digital.
"Adam and Helen were devoted parents, and Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were the light of their lives. Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last forever," the families said.

title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Idaho college massacre survivor says family moved 9 times as strangers followed them
summary: University of Idaho massacre survivor Dylan Mortensen reveals she moved nine times and uses an alias to fight for privacy in the Bryan Kohberger case.
story: Fox News correspondent Natalie Chuck breaks down the defense’s allegations of judicial bias after Kohberger filed a motion to withdraw his guilty plea and disqualify the judge overseeing the case.

The University of Idaho student massacre survivor who came face-to-face with a masked man believed to be Bryan Kohberger is asking a Latah County judge to press pause on an order granting the release of video and images that could show her face in a firsthand letter describing how the trauma has upended her life.

"I worry that even appearing in the background of someone’s photo could lead to more people recognizing me or identifying where I am," Dylan Mortensen wrote in an affidavit to Judge Megan Marshall, asking her to reconsider the order.
Mortensen added that she now uses an alias for delivery orders, at her job and even when introducing herself to new people.
BRYAN KOHBERGER'S COURT HEARINGS ABRUPTLY CANCELED AS LAWYER WARNS OF LENGTHY LEGAL BATTLE
Dylan Mortensen gets a hug after speaking at the sentencing hearing of Bryan Kohberger at the Ada County Courthouse, Wednesday, July 23, 2025, in Boise, Idaho. (Kyle Green/AP via Pool)

"Since November 2022, my family and I have had to move nine times in an effort to protect our privacy and safety," she wrote. "Reporters and strangers investigating the case on their own have shown up outside our homes, followed family members, and invaded our privacy in ways that have made it difficult to feel safe."
Mortensen was one of the first to speak with police after they responded to 1122 King Road in Moscow on Nov. 13, 2022.
Read Dylan Mortensen's affidavit:
She also saw a masked man in her home after the 4 a.m. murders and texted another surviving roommate about it — but didn't call 911.

Police weren't called until around noon, after Mortensen and the other survivor, Bethany Funke, contacted friends who came to the house. One of them saw the remains of their roommate, Xana Kernodle, 20, and her boyfriend, Ethan Chapin, also 20.

"Along with losing four of my friends and experiencing something incredibly traumatic, I have spent nearly four years dealing with public attention, harassment, threats, and constant speculation about my involvement in what happened. People who have never met me have formed opinions about my character, questioned my actions, and accused me of things I had absolutely nothing to do with."
Responding officers also found 21-year-olds Madison Mogen and Kaylee Goncalves dead on the top floor.

Surviving roommate Dylan Mortensen, center with her face blurred, and other University of Idaho students wait to speak with police outside the 1122 King Road crime scene on Nov. 13, 2022. (Moscow Police Department)

"Along with losing four of my friends and experiencing something incredibly traumatic, I have spent nearly four years dealing with public attention, harassment, threats, and constant speculation about my involvement in what happened," Mortensen wrote. "People who have never met me have formed opinions about my character, questioned my actions, and accused me of things I had absolutely nothing to do with."
Read her mother's affidavit:
Later, she wrote, "It is difficult to feel completely comfortable in public when I am constantly considering whether someone knows who I am and what they might believe about me."

What protection she has left, according to her lawyer, is the blur over her face in redacted police video and photographs, and releasing an unblurred version would be an "unwarranted invasion of personal privacy."

Mortensen's attorney, Robyn McPherson, filed a motion to intervene last week after Marshall agreed to the release of previously held records from an independent media company, EWU Media LLC. She is also asking the judge to reconsider the Oct. 20 order and issue a stay until the petition and appeals are resolved.

The motion to reconsider asks Marshall to require Moscow authorities to identify the withheld records, submit them for a private "in-camera" judicial review and prepare a detailed index, arguing that her client can't fully argue for her right to privacy without knowing what the records contain.

She said Moscow's city attorney told her that the documents were expected to include interviews, photographs and videos of Mortensen.
EWU filed a public records request on Aug. 28, 2025, which was at least partially denied. The entity then asked the court to compel the city to disclose them, and Marshall agreed to do so last month.
Read the motion to reconsider:
In another court filing, McPherson wrote that she filed the motion days after learning that Moscow's city attorney did not plan to challenge the decision.

"D.M. seeks reconsideration of the October 20 order only on the issue of whether disclosure of the records withheld by the City [of Moscow] would constitute 'an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy," McPherson wrote.

Madison Mogen, top left, smiles on the shoulders of her best friend, Kaylee Goncalves, as they pose with Ethan Chapin, Xana Kernodle, and two other housemates in Goncalves' final Instagram post, shared the day before the four students were stabbed to death. (@kayleegoncalves/Instagram)

title: NYC woman stabbed while jogging has died as Hochul, Mamdani face questions over unprovoked attacks on women
summary: Two brutal attacks on women in New York City public spaces have leaders under fire, with neither the mayor nor City Council proposing more patrols.
story:
Retired NYPD inspector Paul Mauro weighs in after recent attacks on women across New York City.
He criticizes city leaders’ safety response and says lighting alone won’t be enough. Mauro calls for visible cameras and more proactive policing.

A New York City woman who was stabbed in the neck while jogging last week has died, her family announced Tuesday, as top elected officials face mounting pressure for failing to present a concrete plan of action amid a series of attacks on women in public spaces.

Katie Saurez, 28, died Monday after spending three days on life support after police say an unknown suspect approached her while she was on a run and stabbed her in the neck, which penetrated an artery, the New York Police Department (NYPD) said.
The NYPD told Fox News Digital that Suarez was rushed to the hospital following the attack that happened Friday evening on Shore Parkway Greenway in Brooklyn.
Saurez "sustained multiple stab wounds," police said.
BRUCE BLAKEMAN HAMMERS DEM GOV HOCHUL, MAMDANI OVER SUBWAY SAFETY DURING NYC CAMPAIGN RIDE
The NYPD says Katie Suarez, 28, was stabbed in the neck several times in an unprovoked attack that happened as she was on a run in Brooklyn on a popular jogging and biking path. (NYPD; Google Maps)
Suarez was an avid runner, having completed races with the New York Road Runners. She was jogging to go meet her father when the attack occurred, police said.
"We were sad to hear of this horrible attack — our hearts are with her family and the running community," a spokesperson for the organization said.
Suarez was not registered to run in this past weekend's New York City Marathon.
SMART STREET SENSORS COULD BE WATCHING YOUR CITY NEXT

Responding to the recent violence, a spokesperson for New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said, "Governor Hochul has zero tolerance for violence of any kind and believes any perpetrator must be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Since taking office, the Governor has funded law enforcement at record levels and strengthened bail and discovery laws to hold all violent offenders accountable.
"Governor Hochul's top priority is public safety and she will always fight to protect all New Yorkers."
New York City Council Member Kayla Santosuosso, who represents southern Brooklyn, also responded to the tragedy.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, she said, "I am horrified by the stabbing of Katie Suarez, and first and foremost my thoughts are with Katie and her loving family. I have been personally assured by [NYPD] Commissioner [Jessica] Tisch that the NYPD is pulling out all the stops in their efforts to catch the perpetrator.

"The promenade where this horrific crime took place has been poorly lit for years, since well before I took office. We will be working to ensure that upcoming renovations to the pedestrian bridge near the scene and the promenade itself will include sufficient lighting."
MAMDANI UNVEILS SWEEPING NYPD USE-OF-FORCE REVIEW, BUT STOPS SHORT OF FULFILLING KEY CAMPAIGN PROMISES
An NYPD officer walks towards the area where a woman was reportedly raped at knifepoint inside Central Park. (FNTV)
She called the recent violence against women "deeply disturbing."

Santosuosso went on to say, "We deserve to be able to walk and jog in our neighborhoods without worrying for our safety. This is a serious and personal issue for me as a woman and as a mother and I will be doing everything in my power to keep southern Brooklyn a place where women can live without fear."

Retired NYPD inspector and Fox News contributor Paul Mauro said lighting, in addition to surveillance, needs to be the first step at preventing repeated violence.
"[The] lighting is great, but I would not only ask for that. I would ask for cameras and very ostentatious cameras."
THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?
A 39-year-old woman was raped at knifepoint in Central Park, the NYPD said. (Getty Images: Anadolu; FNTV)

The woman, identified as "Jane Doe" in court documents, sued Caleb T. Suh in New York Supreme Court on Oct. 28, accusing him of assault and battery and seeking damages.
Doe and Suh were cadets at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point when Doe learned she was pregnant in January 2022, according to the complaint.

Doe reported the incident to the Army Criminal Investigation Division at West Point in May 2022.

title: Florida plane crash investigators say weather conditions a 'major focus,' plane may have started to break up
summary: NTSB says the Learjet 60 may have begun breaking apart before the deadly private jet crash in a South Florida neighborhood that killed nine people.
story: National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman said investigators are looking at weather as a "major focus," and said there is evidence that the Learjet that crashed in South Florida was breaking up.
Federal investigators said Monday that weather conditions are a "major focus" of their investigation into the fiery private jet crash that killed nine people in South Florida.

National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) member Tom Chapman said investigators have preliminary indications that the Learjet 60 was breaking apart before it crashed in a Palm Beach County neighborhood Sunday afternoon.

"We do have some indication that the aircraft was breaking up before impact," Chapman said during a Monday news conference. "And so, some of this has yet to be determined. We may find parts of the aircraft some distance away from the actual impact site."
COPILOT KILLED IN FIERY FLORIDA LEARJET CRASH IDENTIFIED AS 20-YEAR-OLD WHO LEARNED TO FLY BEFORE DRIVING
Police work near the scene of a plane crash in Greenacres, Fla., Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)
Chapman said investigators are also examining the weather conditions the jet encountered at approximately 35,000 feet, where the crew reported icing and moderate turbulence shortly before the crash.

"The weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation," Chapman said. "You all saw what the weather was like here at the surface. What we have to determine is what the weather conditions were like at altitude."

The aircraft departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas around 10:37 a.m. Sunday, bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas with two crew members and seven passengers aboard, according to the NTSB.
At approximately 12:47 p.m., the crew reported encountering manageable light clear ice and moderate turbulence, with altitude deviations of roughly 700 feet while flying at 35,000 feet.
The crew also reported an outside temperature of minus 47 degrees Celsius, or minus 53 degrees Fahrenheit, before requesting permission to climb to 37,000 feet after encountering precipitation.
Flames rise following an aircraft incident in Palm Beach County, Florida. (Eduin Cruz/via REUTERS)
Air traffic control approved the request, but less than 30 seconds later, the crew reported descending and issued a mayday call around 12:48 p.m.
"We are in an overspeed condition, descending," the crew transmitted, according to Chapman, who said the remainder of the message was unintelligible.

Subsequent communications indicated the jet was rapidly losing altitude before it crashed into a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, around 12:50 p.m., killing all nine people aboard.
NTSB investigator-in-charge Timothy Manville said the on-scene investigation will take several days, with recovering the wreckage from a crater in the roadway posing a significant challenge.
"The biggest obstacle that we're going to have is recovering the major wreckage from the impacted crater on the roadway," Manville said.
Dashcam footage captured the jet plunging nose-first into the neighborhood and erupting into a massive fireball, as Fox News Digital previously reported.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis described the crash as "cataclysmic" Sunday, saying the aircraft "looked like a missile going down" and left a large crater beside the road.
The crash also prompted the evacuation of approximately 600 people from a nearby mobile home community, according to local officials.

title: Christa Pike's execution doctor says misplaced IV sent lethal drugs into her arms instead of veins
summary: Dr. Mark Fowler reveals an improperly placed IV sent pentobarbital into Christa Pike's tissue instead of her bloodstream during the failed execution.
story: Anesthesiologist Dr. Joel Zivot joins Bill Hemmer to discuss the legal fallout after a judge ordered Tennessee officials to preserve evidence from the botched execution of Christa Pike. Zivot, who advised Pike's attorneys, explains the complications surrounding the lethal injection drugs used in the state's attempt. Pike remains on death row following the failed execution attempt.

The doctor who participated in Christa Pike's failed execution in Tennessee says an improperly placed IV sent lethal drugs into the tissue of her arms instead of her bloodstream — and acknowledged the execution team should have stopped when the death row inmate complained of pain.
Dr. Mark Fowler, who served as the physician during Pike's Sept. 30 execution attempt, offered a rare firsthand account of what went wrong in an interview with New York Magazine published Friday.
Pike, 50, survived after receiving two doses of pentobarbital and was hospitalized for days before eventually regaining consciousness.
TENNESSEE DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES IN FAILED EXECUTION ATTEMPT
The doctor told the magazine he knew something was wrong when Pike's execution stretched to about 45 minutes. When he was called into the chamber, she was still alive and gasping for air.

An execution gurney is shown alongside a Tennessee Department of Correction booking photo of death row inmate Christa Pike, whose attorneys filed an emergency motion seeking to preserve evidence after the state's failed execution attempt. (Greg Smith/CORBIS/Corbis via Getty Images ; Tennessee Department of Correction via AP)
Fowler said he initially considered whether Pike's response to the medication could simply be taking longer than expected and decided to give it more time.
DEATH ROW INMATE UNCONSCIOUS ON VENTILATOR AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION FOR TEEN’S KILLING: ATTORNEYS

As another half-hour passed, he became concerned that Pike could survive with irreversible brain damage. Fowler later diagnosed her as comatose before a deputy commissioner ordered the execution stopped.
He then ordered oxygen, and Pike was taken by ambulance to Vanderbilt University Medical Center.
911 OPERATORS QUESTIONED WHETHER CHRISTA PIKE FAILED EXECUTION CALL WAS PRANK, AUDIO REVEALS
Fowler told New York Magazine that the IV used to administer the pentobarbital had not been properly inserted into Pike's veins.
"It was delivering medicine to the subcutaneous tissue" of her arms, Fowler said.

Convicted killer Christa Gail Pike listens to proceedings on April 2008 in Knox County Criminal Court in a bid for a new trial in the 1995 killing of fellow Job Corps student Colleen Slemmer. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)
DEATH ROW KILLER CHRISTA PIKE DESCRIBES WAKING UP AFTER EXECUTION SHE NEVER EXPECTED TO SURVIVE
Pike's attorneys previously said in a court filing that she complained of severe arm pain during the execution, telling those in the chamber, "My arm feels like it’s about to burst open."
"They should have stopped and reassessed, and they didn’t," Fowler told New York Magazine.
CHRISTA PIKE'S ATTORNEY SAYS SHE'S 'UP AND WALKING' MORE THAN A WEEK AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION
The account comes days after Pike described the aftermath of the failed execution in a statement released by her attorneys, saying she remains in constant pain and still struggles to speak.
"My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts," Pike said Friday. "I still struggle to speak."
Pike also said she was "deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position."
Fowler's role in Pike's failed execution was not his first to draw scrutiny.
CHRISTA PIKE EXECUTION FAILURE SPARES MURDERER WHO BAILED VICTIM OUT JUST TO KILL HIM
Christa Gail Pike appears remotely from Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation for her hearing in Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tenn., on Aug. 11, 2026. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)
New York Magazine reported that Fowler was also involved in the 2025 execution of Byron Black and the failed May execution of Tony Carruthers.

In the Carruthers case, Fowler attempted to place an IV near Carruthers' clavicle after paramedics were unable to establish traditional IV access. Fowler told the magazine he ultimately stopped because he lacked adequate anesthetic and the procedure was becoming too painful for Carruthers.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
"I'm not an evil, vicious person. I'm not unscrupulous. I'm not uncaring, and I'm not incompetent," Fowler said.
Still, Fowler said Tennessee's lethal-injection protocol needs to change.
He called for fewer handoffs among execution team members and said those responsible for placing IV lines should remain in position to monitor them as the lethal drugs are administered.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
"The people who place the IV lines should thereafter be observant about what’s happening with them as the medicine goes in," Fowler said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
A split image shows Christa Pike at her murder trial in 1995, left, and Colleen Slemmer, the young woman she was convicted of torturing and killing, on the right. (Reuters)
Following the failed execution, Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee halted the state's remaining executions for the year and ordered an independent review of what went wrong.
SEND US A TIP
Lee said last week that Pike remains incarcerated under state law and signaled that her death sentence is unlikely to change.
GOT A TIP?
"I suspect her sentence will be the same as it was before unless determined otherwise by the courts," Lee said.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow participant in a federal Job Corps program in Knoxville.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
Pike's attorneys have called on Lee to commute her death sentence to life without parole.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Fowler and the Tennessee Department of Correction seeking additional comment and an interview but has not received a response.

title: George Floyd-era police watchdog chair charged with selling name to inmate who vowed to 'blow down' witness
summary: Hassan Bennett, chair of Philadelphia's police watchdog, allegedly sold a witness' name in an attempted murder case to a man who vowed violence.
story: National Police Association spokeswoman Sgt. Betsy Brantner Smith says Philadelphia officials should scrutinize the city’s police oversight commission after its chair was accused of selling sensitive case information to a prison inmate.
The chair of Philadelphia's city-run police watchdog is accused of selling a witness' name in an attempted murder case to a man who threatened to "blow down the witness in broad daylight."

Hassan Bennett, chair of the Philadelphia Citizens Police Oversight Commission, faces charges after investigators say he sold a witness' name and an unredacted arrest report to a prison inmate in a domestic violence attempted murder case to Thomas Scott, who allegedly vowed to "blow down" the witness "in broad daylight." Bennett also works at the Defender Association of Philadelphia.

Investigators listened to prison calls and heard Bennett read Scott details from the arrest report in the attempted murder case, the Philadelphia District Attorney's Office said in a news release. Bennett also allegedly handed over the witness' full name.
MADISON BROOKS RAPE SUSPECT'S ATTORNEY HELD IN CONTEMPT FOR USING HER NAME TO TRY TO BAN PINK IN COURTROOM

Philadelphia police watchdog chair Hassan Bennett allegedly provided prison inmate Thomas Scott with sensitive information from an attempted murder case, including a witness’ full name, prosecutors said. (Citizens Police Oversight Commission)

Scott then asked Bennett for a copy of the paperwork, offering to pay him $500, officials said. The documents were sent to Scott, who sent them to various other people "in order to intimidate the witness in the open case," the district attorney's office said.
The district attorney's office said Scott was recorded saying he "was searching for the witness' location, that the witness needs to recant his statement."
LUIGI MANGIONE JUDGE SAYS JURORS WILL REMAIN ANONYMOUS AFTER THREATS AND HARASSMENT OF WITNESSES
Officials say Scott was recorded saying "the whole purpose of his social media posts was to prevent the witness from coming to court."

Bennett, who now leads the Citizens Police Oversight Commission, a body formed after the 2020 protests over George Floyd's death, was convicted of second-degree murder in 2008. He was acquitted at a 2019 retrial, where one of the victims and a co-defendant testified that their earlier statements implicating him had been coerced by a then-homicide detective.
EMBATTLED SOROS-BACKED DA BLAMES ‘CRIMINAL’ POLICE MISCONDUCT IN ACCUSED PHILLY COP KILLER’S PRIOR MURDER CASE

Hassan Bennett, chair of Philadelphia’s Citizens Police Oversight Commission, is accused of selling an unredacted arrest report and a witness’ identity to prison inmate Thomas Scott, according to prosecutors. (Citizens Police Oversight Commission)
Both men face felony charges of intimidation of witness/victim, conspiracy, criminal use of communication facility and bribery.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
National Police Association spokeswoman Sgt. Betsy Brantner Smith told Fox News Digital that the incident should be a "cautionary tale" for other cities.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

"When you are given that much access to people's private information, and you are giving that much access to inside information, the city in this case needs to be very sure that he is someone who is ethical," Smith said. "Just because you have had a felony conviction overturned doesn't mean that you have the ethics necessary to handle this sensitive information."
SEND US A TIP
"We believe that this entire commission in Philadelphia needs to be looked at, each person individually," she added.
District Attorney Larry Krasner said Bennett's alleged crimes are "serious" but "not a reflection on the work of the Citizens Police Oversight Commission or the Defender Association of Philadelphia."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner attends a news conference on Dec. 30, 2019 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Mark Makela/Getty Images)
"I would like to be in a position to say that this defendant had no such involvement, but he did, and the evidence is strong," Krasner said.
DEM JUSTICES SLAP SOROS-BACKED PHILLY DA WITH POWER STRIP IN STUNNING DECISION: 'NOT RELIABLE'
In a statement, the Philadelphia Citizens Police Oversight Commission said Bennett is on leave.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We recognize the seriousness of this matter. We will respect the legal process, refrain from commenting on legal allegations that are under investigation and take appropriate steps to protect confidential information," the commission said. "Our responsibility to the people of Philadelphia remains unchanged. We will continue our work to strengthen police accountability, promote transparency, and build public trust."
Fox News Digital reached out to Scott's attorney. Bennett could not immediately be reached for comment.
Adam Sabes is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Adam.Sabes@fox.com and on Twitter @asabes10.

title: Missing Utah teen Kylie Arellano found safe in Oregon after 500-day search
summary: Kylie Arellano was found safe in Oregon with a 39-year-old man after vanishing from Utah more than 500 days ago, ending a massive FBI search.
story: Missing Utah teen Kylie Arellano has been found safe in Oregon after 500-day search.
A Utah teenager who vanished nearly a year and a half ago has been found safe in Oregon, ending a lengthy nationwide search that spanned more than 500 days.
Kylie Arellano, now 17, was last seen by her family on May 29, 2025, at their home in Garden City, Utah, when she was 15 years old.
Kylie's disappearance had triggered a wide federal and state investigation that led officials through dozens of unconfirmed sightings before culminating in her recovery on Sunday.
MISSING TEEN FOUND HIDING IN CONVICTED SEX OFFENDER'S CLOSET IN FLORIDA, SHERIFF SAYS
Kylie Arellano was reported missing in 2025 and was found with a 39-year-old man in Oregon. (Rich County Sheriff's Office / Facebook)

Law enforcement officers in Oregon, working directly with the FBI's Salt Lake City field office and the Rich County Sheriff's Office, safely recovered the teen, according to a law enforcement news release.
Kylie, they said, was found with a 39-year-old man in Oregon. The man was taken into custody without incident.
"The FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the U.S. and in other countries.
FBI NABS MORE THAN 350 ALLEGED CHILD SEX ABUSE OFFENDERS
Federal government office in Salt Lake City, Utah. (Google Maps)
"As this case is ongoing, no further information will be released at this time," the FBI's Salt Lake City field office said in a statement on Sunday.
Federal authorities also credited the Oregon State Police, the FBI's Portland field office and the Utah Department of Public Safety for their assistance in the operation.

"Tonight, local police in Oregon brought a minor who had been missing for a year and a half to safety, acting on information provided by our FBI Salt Lake City Field Office," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital.
"We are grateful she can return home, and we will continue working with our partners to hold those responsible accountable," Patel added.
MIKE WALTZ, TIM TEBOW LAUNCH EFFORT TO COMBAT ONLINE CHILD EXPLOITATION: 'IT'S HAPPENING IN THEIR BACKYARD'
Weeks before her rescue, Kylie Arellano's mother marked the 500-day milestone online. (Rich County Sheriff's Office / Facebook)
"To anyone using gore groups to target and exploit children: the FBI and our partners are coming for you.
"We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice and protect America’s children."

Kylie Arellano’s grandmother also thanked the authorities for finding her. "THANK YOU for all you and your agents and teams are doing to find our baby girl, Kylie Arellano and bring her home!!!" she wrote on X.
According to a law enforcement source, the suspect allegedly met the teenager on Snapchat before her disappearance.
Last year, Rich County Sheriff Dale Stacey said detectives had chased reports of sightings across multiple states and urged the public to preserve any photographic or timestamped evidence.
TWO MISSING CHILDREN RESCUED FROM TRAILER AS POLICE ARREST BABYSITTER ON KIDNAPPING CHARGES
Kylie Arellano was found with a male suspect who was taken into custody after a search spanning multiple states. (Rich County Sheriff's Office / Facebook)
New details about the investigation had also emerged days before Kylie was found.

Unsealed search warrants reviewed by KUTV on Oct. 29 showed that investigators had previously scrutinized Kylie's mother, Stephanie Coleman, and questioned her about a 2024 allegation of physical abuse.
There were also questions about discrepancies involving missing text messages from the night Kylie vanished and suspicious marks in the home.
Coleman had denied having any role in her daughter's disappearance or abusing her, providing timestamped "good night" text messages from May 29, 2025.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
She said the marks were caused by an injured cat and maintained that Kylie had likely been groomed and lured away by someone she encountered online, the outlet reported.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Savannah Guthrie makes heartbreaking plea in mom's disappearance after finding old drawing
summary: Savannah Guthrie shared her daughter's emotional drawing in a new plea for answers nine months after Nancy Guthrie vanished from her Tucson home.
story: Lisa Miller, a retired detective and law enforcement executive at the Colorado Attorney General's Office, breaks down some of the unique attributes of the purported ransom note.
"TODAY" co-host Savannah Guthrie issued a new plea for information about her missing mother, Nancy Guthrie, on Sunday, nine months after the 84-year-old was abducted from her Tucson, Arizona, home.
Guthrie shared an old drawing made by her daughter, Vale, showing a blue umbrella in the rain and the words, "I know it might not seem like it, but I really need my mommy."
"Found this old drawing from my daughter today," Guthrie wrote on Instagram. "It says so much about how I feel."
"The world goes on, things appear ‘normal’ — as we try to keep going and be strong, especially for our young kids — but it’s not and it never will be," she continued.
SAVANNAH GUTHRIE URGES PUBLIC TO HELP FIND MISSING MOTHER NANCY IN EMOTIONAL MOTHER’S DAY POST

A photo of Nancy Guthrie, NBC host Savannah Guthrie's mother, which Savannah Guthrie posted to Instagram on Aug 1, 2026. Nancy Guthrie went missing in February. Her children have pleaded with the public for help identifying her kidnappers after the Pima County Sheriff’s Department released released a pair of ransom notes. (Savannah Guthrie/ Instagram)
"For Annie and Tommy, for Cam and Kristine, for Mike and me and for all of Mom’s beloved grandchildren: We ache for her, we cry out for answers, we cannot move forward," Guthrie wrote.

"We need someone to help us, tell us what you know. Our mom was a light in this world. We want to celebrate her and give her the dignity she deserves. The reward is still available. Please. We are begging you. Please help us."
Guthrie also thanked those who have supported her family and urged people to "join us in praying without ceasing."
THREE MONTHS AFTER NANCY GUTHRIE'S ABDUCTION, SHERIFF'S OFFICE RENEWS PLEA AS KEY QUESTIONS REMAIN UNANSWERED
Savannah Guthrie and her mother, Nancy Guthrie. (Instagram/Savannah Guthrie)
Nancy Guthrie was reported missing Feb. 1 after she was last seen at her home in the Catalina Foothills area near Tucson shortly before 10 p.m. Jan. 31.
Authorities believe she was taken against her will.
A masked, armed individual was captured on the home's doorbell camera footage, apparently tampering with the device.
The FBI and Pima County Sheriff’s Department have not identified a suspect, and no arrests have been made.
SAVANNAH GUTHRIE WAS 'SURPRISED AND DISMAYED' BY DOUBTS SHE WOULD RETURN TO 'TODAY' AFTER MOM'S DISAPPEARANCE
The home of Nancy Guthrie, the missing mother of "TODAY" show host Savannah Guthrie, is seen from above, Thursday, Feb. 5, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. (Caitlin O'Hara/AP Photo)
Guthrie has continued to push for answers about her mother’s disappearance while returning to work on "TODAY."
During a June appearance on "TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle," she rejected the idea that she had forgotten about her mother.
"I know maybe people wonder, ‘What’s going on? How is she able to do that job? Is she not thinking about it? Did she forget?’ No. Never," Guthrie said.
"It’s always with me. I cry every morning on the way to work, and I cry every morning on the way home," she added.
SAVANNAH GUTHRIE DELIVERS 'VERY SPECIFIC' MESSAGE TO MOM'S KIDNAPPER 25 WEEKS AFTER HER ABDUCTION
Savannah Guthrie and her mother, Nancy Guthrie. (Instagram/Savannah Guthrie)
In August, six months after her mother's disappearance, Guthrie and her siblings also issued a statement asking for information about their mother.

"Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on — because that’s what our joyful and resilient Mom taught us to do. But make no mistake — our hearts are in ruins," Guthrie wrote. "Cam and Kristine, Annie and Tommy, Mike and me — we spend every waking moment thinking of her, longing for her, looking for her."
The Pima County Sheriff’s Department said Friday the Nancy Guthrie Task Force was continuing to work with laboratories to advance DNA analysis.

"Earlier this month, investigators traveled to Florida to meet with lab scientists to see what more could be done to advance this case," the department wrote on X. "A number of ideas were discussed, and we continue to work with all our partners to solve this case."
The agency reminded the public that no tip is too small.
Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos previously said Guthrie "did not leave on her own."
NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

A supportive sign left by neighbors is posted outside the home of Nancy Guthrie, the 84-year-old mother of television host Savannah Guthrie, who went missing from her home in Tucson, Arizona, U.S. February 4, 2026. (Rebecca Noble/Reuters)
Authorities released the contents of two ransom notes in July. The first, sent Feb. 2, claimed Guthrie was safe and demanded $4 million in bitcoin for her release.
The second, sent four days later, claimed she had died shortly after being kidnapped.
Investigators said the notes contained distinctive writing patterns and asked anyone who recognized the style to contact authorities.
A possible additional ransom text message reported in September was later deemed not credible by investigators.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Anyone with information is asked to call the FBI at 1-800-CALL-FBI or submit an anonymous tip at 520-882-7463.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Private jet with 9 people on board crashes just miles from Mar-a-Lago
summary: A small plane carrying nine people crashed and exploded in Palm Beach County, Florida, just miles from Mar-a-Lago.
story: Video from a car on the road shows the Learjet going down near Cresthaven, Florida. Nine people were aboard the plane, which was bound for the Bahamas; the FAA and NTSB are investigating. (Credit: Aki Kuusisto via Storyful)
All nine people on board a private jet that crashed around nine miles from President Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach County, Florida are dead.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy shared the update Sunday afternoon, calling the incident a "horrific tragedy."

"The FAA is sending a team to the scene to support the @NTSB's investigation. Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost —@FAANews & @USDOT are closely monitoring this crash and will share updates as we learn more," he added in a post on social media.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) confirmed that the Learjet 60 crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, around 12:50 p.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1.
'WE THOUGHT WE WOULD DIE': PASSENGERS THROWN INTO CEILING DURING TERRIFYING FLIGHT
A Learjet 60 crashed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday afternoon. (Palm Beach County Fire Rescue)
The jet departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, according to the agency.
No word yet on the identities of the nine people killed on board the jet.
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED
A Learjet 60 slammed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday afternoon, erupting into a massive fireball just nine miles from Mar-a-Lago. (Aki Kuusisto via Storyful)
Emergency crews shut down Military Trail between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, warning the public to avoid the area.
UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT
"Aircraft Incident," Palm Beach County Fire Rescue said on X. "Avoid the area. This will be an extended incident."
The fiery crash was captured on dashcam video. The jet can be seen rapidly descending from the sky before crashing nose-first into the ground and immediately exploding into a massive fireball.
Emergency crews shut down Military Trail between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, warning the public to avoid the area as flames consumed the wreckage. (Aki Kuusisto via Storyful)
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis later described the crash as "cataclysmic," telling reporters the plane crash in Palm Beach "looked like a missile going down."
"It left a big crater on the side of the road," he said.

"There was a lot of debris that was spewed as a result of this crash. As of now, we don't have any reports of anyone who was on the ground apart from the people in the plane who were killed or injured as a result of the debris," he said.
"But the debris was significant, and it went over a pretty significant distance. I've received a briefing from the county officials.
"We've also been in contact with the FAA. There will be some folks here. Obviously, they do an investigation in situations like these."
DEADLY CRASH KILLS TWO AS PLANE PLUNGES INTO 'BALL OF FLAMES' NEAR SUBURBAN GOLF COURSE
Flames rise from a crater in the road after the private jet crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida.  ( Eduin Cruz/via REUTERS)
The impact displaced residents living near a mobile home park.
District 3 Commissioner Joel Flores also said officials were working to ensure that about 600 people affected by the crash had a safe place to stay Sunday night.
"We got the Red Cross and stood by, making sure that we provided just initial services for them.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"So I think that's our worry right now, making sure that those folks have somewhere to go to stay safe with them," he said before explaining that the crash site was at the entrance to a mobile home park.
"Unfortunately, that's a crime scene. They're investigating that, so the people can't stay there. We are relocating them to two shelters in the county. They're on standby."

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Shootings near 5 college communities leave 3 dead, at least 29 injured
summary: A violent Halloween across the U.S. leaves police investigating five shootings near college campuses in Indiana, Delaware, Alabama, Illinois and Colorado, while Dallas shootings leave four dead.
story: Birmingham police said one person was killed and eight others were wounded near Legion Field after the Alabama A&M–Alabama State game Saturday.
Shootings in four college communities over the weekend left three people dead and at least 29 others injured.
Indiana, Delaware, Alabama, Illinois and Colorado police are each investigating shootings in crowded parties near college communities, according to police and university statements.

Seven were hospitalized in Bloomington, Indiana, near Indiana University's homecoming, while the University of Delaware is still counting victims (six are reportedly hospitalized) and the Magic City Classic football game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State near Legion Field in Birmingham, Alabama, left at least one dead and eight wounded.

In Bloomington, Illinois, eight people were shot near Illinois Wesleyan University, leaving a 19-year-old woman dead. A shooting in Boulder, Colorado, left one University of Colorado Boulder student dead and another critically injured.
SHOOTING AFTER MAGIC CITY CLASSIC IN ALABAMA LEAVES 1 DEAD, 8 INJURED

People in Halloween costumes cross Main Street as police close several blocks in downtown Newark after a shooting on Halloween night Saturday. (William Bretzger/Delaware News Journal/USA Today Network via Imagn Images)

After midnight near Indiana University, officers monitoring a large crowd around Kirkwood Avenue and Dunn Street heard shots around 1:30 a.m. ET and saw a man with a firearm running from the area, Bloomington police said.
Officers took the man into custody near Dunn Meadow, and recovered a gun and shell casings in the area. Police said it remains unclear whether the suspect fired any shots.
No deaths were reported in Bloomington, and police said they did not know whether there were additional victims.
FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING LEAVES 12 INJURED, INCLUDING 6 CHILDREN, NEAR FOOTBALL STADIUM
A disturbance in the crowd may have preceded the shooting, police said. Indiana University police and Indiana State Police assisted in the response.
In Newark, Delaware, a shooting on Saturday night rocked the University of Delaware.

"We are deeply concerned about the shooting on Main Street Saturday night, which has impacted our entire community," Delaware's VP for Public Affairs Rick Deadwyler told Fox News Digital in a statement. "We are grateful to the Newark Police Department, which is leading the investigation. We will continue to communicate confirmed information, which will be shared on a dedicated alerts page (udel.edu/about/alerts) and updated as we learn more."
University President Laura Carlson said victims were receiving care and thanked Newark police, campus police and other first responders for providing on-scene care.
POLICE OFFICER, WOMAN SHOT NEAR NOTRE DAME AFTER FOOTBALL TAILGATES

"I am writing to you about the shooting last night in Newark on Main Street, although it is difficult to know what to say when violence like this erupts in our community," she wrote in an email to the school community.

"We are all impacted," she continued. "I ask that you keep the victims in your thoughts and hearts as they receive care. Please also recognize the impact and toll on our students and community members who were on Main Street last night and witnessed this violence."

The university did not provide a confirmed number of victims or say whether anyone had died, but a report indicated at least six were hospitalized. The investigation is being led by Newark police. The school urged students and staff to follow its campus alerts page for confirmed updates.

In Birmingham, Alabama, one person was killed and eight others were wounded Saturday night after the Magic City Classic football game near Legion Field, police said. Officers found nine people with gunshot wounds in the 400 block of Graymont Avenue West shortly after 7:50 p.m. ET.
SEVERAL UNIVERSITY OF IOWA STUDENTS WOUNDED IN DOWNTOWN SHOOTING AFTER FIGHT ERUPTS NEAR CAMPUS
One victim was in critical condition and seven others were stable, authorities said.

Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, said most spectators and families had left the stadium property after the game, but the shooting happened nearby, where vendors were set up along Graymont Avenue.
He said he was "very grateful that more people weren’t injured."
Police spokesperson De'Rell Freeman said one person had been detained and transported to police headquarters for questioning, and "multiple weapons" had been found and secured.

Alabama State and Alabama A&M are historically Black universities and archrivals whose annual contest has been played for more than 100 years. Nearly 70,000 fans attended Saturday's game, won by Alabama A&M 31-28. The event draws some of the largest crowds in the country for games played in their college football division.
The Magic City Classic has such a deep history that Alabama State coach Eddie Robinson Jr., a former NFL linebacker and alumnus of the school, proposed creating a Hall of Fame for the game.
POLICE MAKE ARREST AFTER GUNFIRE DURING CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME LEAVES 1 DEAD
Emergency personnel work at the scene of a shooting incident, in Birmingham, Alabama, Oct. 31, 2026. (Jokerta Horne via Reuters)
In Bloomington, Illinois, police responded just before 1:25 a.m. Sunday to a shooting near Illinois Wesleyan University and found multiple people at the scene with gunshot wounds.

Officers immediately secured the scene with assistance from the Illinois State Police and McLean County Sheriff's Office, and seven victims were taken to the hospital for treatment. A 19-year-old woman was pronounced dead at the scene by the McLean County Coroner's Office and another woman remains in critical condition.
ATF Chicago confirmed Sunday afternoon that it is assisting with the investigation.
SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR SUSPECTED GUNMAN OUTSIDE NOTRE DAME FOOTBALL GAME VS MICHIGAN STATE
In Boulder, Colorado, an overnight shooting on University Hill killed one University of Colorado Boulder student and left another critically injured.

Just before 11:30 p.m. Saturday, Boulder police officers responded to a home for a reported shooting. Officers arrived at the scene in less than two minutes and found two 19-year-old men with gunshot wounds. Both were taken to the hospital where one was pronounced dead. The second victim remains in critical condition.

Both victims were University of Colorado Boulder students, and the Boulder County Coroner's Office will release the identity of the victim who died, according to a news release from the city of Boulder.

Officials said the shooting report was the second call to the home Saturday night. Earlier Saturday night, Boulder police responded to a noise complaint involving a large party at the home. Officers contacted the people who lived at the home and cited them for having a nuisance party. Following police intervention, the party ended, and hundreds of attendees left the area. A smaller group remained inside the home.
Detectives said they believe a group of people later attempted to force their way into the house. Shortly after that scuffle, shots were fired inside the home, striking the two victims.
Detectives have interviewed roughly 20 witnesses and continue to pursue numerous leads, according to the city.

Detectives released photos of two persons of interest and other possible witnesses. The first person of interest was described as a man with short, dark hair and facial hair, wearing a red hooded sweatshirt underneath a black jacket. The second person of interest was described as a man with short, dark hair, wearing a black shirt with Art the Clown on it and a silver chain necklace.

"My heart breaks for the victims and for everyone impacted by this senseless violence. Our community deserves to feel safe, and we will not accept this kind of violence in Boulder," Boulder Police Chief Steve Redfearn wrote in a statement. "I want to assure these families and our community that we are doing everything in our power to find those responsible and hold them accountable."

In addition to the shootings near campuses, police in Dallas say four people are dead and 15 are injured following three separate shootings in a Dallas neighborhood. Police Chief Daniel Comeaux said police are still trying to determine if the shootings were related or what led to them. Comeaux said some arrests were made, but he did not specify how many or what charges were involved.

"This is a really big scene. It's spread out," Comeaux said. "We are interviewing some individuals right now that we have arrested, still trying to figure out exactly how it ties into all the shootings out here."

In Fayetteville, Arkansas, six people were taken to hospitals with gunshot wounds from a shooting that happened early Sunday. No arrests have been made, police said in a news release. A preliminary investigation indicates an altercation preceded the shooting.
Fox News' Bradford Betz and Angelica Stabile and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Wyoming mom reported missing after not picking up kids; sister, police search for answers
summary: Kandice Gunter's phone last pinged near Highway 387 in Natrona County after the 30-year-old mother failed to pick up her kids from Boys & Girls Club.
story: Kandice Gunter, 30, a 5-foot-7 white female around 185 pounds with black hair and blue eyes, was last seen in person on the morning of Oct. 29, 2026 in Natrona County. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images; Casper Police Department)
A Wyoming mother of two has been reported missing for days after she failed to pick up her children from an after-school program, prompting her sister to raise the alarm.

Kandice Gunter, 30, was last seen Thursday morning in Natrona County, according to the Casper Police Department. Her sister, Kayla Gunter, told Cowboy State Daily she reported her missing after Kandice did not collect her children, ages 9 and 6, from the Boys & Girls Club on Wednesday.
"That's why I started freaking out," Kayla told the paper. "It's totally out of character for her not to show up to get her kids."
FAMILY OF CRITICALLY MISSING DC MOTHER SAYS POLICE STILL TREATING HOME AS ACTIVE CRIME SCENE
Kandice Gunter, 30, a mother of two, is mysteriously missing before Halloween, leaving a grieving family to celebrate the holiday without their mother. (FOX)

Police said Gunter was last known to be traveling in a gray 2016 GMC Canyon pickup with a Wyoming temporary registration. Her cellphone was last located around 12:30 p.m. MT on Friday along Highway 387, near the Natrona County line.

The sisters last spoke by phone at 10:41 a.m. local time Wednesday. Kayla said the conversation gave no indication anything was wrong, and Gunter stopped answering calls afterward. The family was also told her phone pinged near Gillette around noon Wednesday, according to the report.
Gunter had reportedly moved from Nevada to Casper about a month earlier to be closer to her children. She had been staying with their father and helping care for them.
BAHAMIAN AUTHORITIES APPROVE SEARCH OF 25-FOOT-DEEP ZONE FLAGGED BY BRIAN HOOKER'S PHONE GPS DATA: SOURCES

"I looked so hard but there’s so much wide open spaces with one set of sad eyes hope you’re okay!! 14 years you’ve been in my life and can’t end it like this Kandice Gunter," Facebook user TK Kentopp posted early Saturday morning.
NEW YORK GRANDMOTHER VANISHES IN LAS VEGAS AS FAMILY GETS MYSTERIOUS TEXTS FROM HER PHONE ASKING FOR BITCOIN

In the days before she disappeared, Gunter posted on Facebook: "Success for me, happens in silence." She had also written in June about "focusing on a better me. Again," alongside a heart-mending emoji.
Kayla said the move appeared to be going well and her sister had not indicated she planned to leave or cut off contact. The sisters typically spoke by phone at least three times a day.
Gunter was last seen in person on the morning of Oct. 29 in Natrona County and was reported missing to police later that evening, the Casper Police Department said.
Gunter is described as 5 feet 7 inches tall and weighing about 185 pounds, with black hair and blue eyes. She has a butterfly tattoo on her neck.

Anyone who has seen Gunter or the pickup, or has information about her whereabouts, is asked to call the Casper Police Department at 307-235-8278. Anonymous tips can be submitted to Crime Stoppers of Central Wyoming at 307-577-8477 or at crimestopperscasper.org.
